submission.name: Reserve Relay
submission.tagline: Turn small purchase roundups into a shared emergency reserve, with a live view of the work behind each suggestion.
submission.inspiration: We were interested in making it easier for community groups to build a modest cash buffer from everyday activity. We paired automated roundup calculations with the idea of a coordinated agent team that can explain and check a financial workflow.
submission.what_it_does: Reserve Relay reads sample transactions, calculates the difference to the next dollar, and shows how those amounts could build a reserve. A small set of AI agents handles transaction categorization, summarizes spending patterns, and flags items that need review; the app can also send a simulated transfer to a Solana Devnet wallet.
submission.how_we_built_it: A FastAPI service connects a Nessie transaction feed, roundup calculations, Gemini-generated summaries, and Solana Devnet transfers to a React dashboard. We used separate agent roles for categorization, insight writing, and review, and stream their status to the interface so users can see which step is running.
submission.challenges_we_ran_into: The complete demo runs with sample data, but categorization sometimes assigns a transaction to the wrong spending group, which can skew the generated advice. We also found that tiny decimal amounts need careful conversion before they become token units.
submission.accomplishments: We connected the sample transaction flow to roundup totals, an AI explanation, and a testnet transfer. The live agent activity view helped us make the otherwise hidden processing steps easier to follow.
submission.what_we_learned: We learned that multiple AI roles are useful only when their handoffs and outputs are easy to inspect. Gemini helped draft plain-language summaries, while we learned to keep calculations and transfer amounts in deterministic code.
submission.whats_next: We would improve categorization review, add configurable reserve goals, and support more transaction sources. Before any real financial use, we would also need stronger security and a careful review of transfer and account requirements.
